sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的那个黑胶唱片时代，你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 然后把DJ台变成一个鲜活的、快闪式的博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: Previously, on The Daily.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《每日新闻》。上期回顾：

sentences.en: How big was your staff pre-pandemic, and how big is it now?
sentences.zh: 疫情前你们有多少员工，现在又有多少？

sentences.en: So in February, I believe we had about 13 employees.
sentences.zh: 二月份的时候，我想我们大约有13名员工。

sentences.en: Now it's six of us.
sentences.zh: 现在只剩下我们六个了。

sentences.en: Pre-pandemic, we had a staff close to 50.
sentences.zh: 疫情前，我们的员工人数接近50人。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: What do you have now?
sentences.zh: 现在还有多少？

sentences.en: I have 30 now.
sentences.zh: 现在有30人。

sentences.en: Over the past two years, tens of millions of Americans quit their jobs.
sentences.zh: 在过去两年里，数千万美国人辞去了工作。

sentences.en: You know, and started thinking, like, well, why am I really doing this?
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们开始思考：我到底为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: It felt very liberating.
sentences.zh: 这感觉非常令人解脱。

sentences.en: I was able to rediscover and discover things that I never really did for myself.
sentences.zh: 我能够重新发现并探索那些我从未真正为自己做过的事情。

sentences.en: Is this really serving me, or is it just serving, you know, whoever my employer is?
sentences.zh: 这真的是为了我好，还是仅仅为了我的雇主？

sentences.en: It was a tidal wave that became known as the Great Resignation.
sentences.zh: 这股浪潮后来被称为“大辞职潮”。

sentences.en: For now, I would much rather take my time and try to find a situation where there's stability and security.
sentences.zh: 目前，我宁愿花点时间，努力寻找一个稳定且有保障的环境。

sentences.en: Once I took stock of my life, I was like, I've never, ever, ever.
sentences.zh: 当我审视自己的生活时，我心想，我从来、从来、从来没有过。

sentences.en: They're gone.
sentences.zh: 他们走了。

sentences.en: Ever.
sentences.zh: 再也不会了。

sentences.en: They're not coming back.
sentences.zh: 他们不会回来了。

sentences.en: Ever, ever, ever going back to that.
sentences.zh: 再也不会、不会、不会回到那种状态了。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people are like, I've had it.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人都在想：我受够了。

sentences.en: I'm done with it.
sentences.zh: 我不想再干了。

sentences.en: I can't do it anymore.
sentences.zh: 我再也坚持不下去了。

sentences.en: I think it's a wake-up call.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个警钟。

sentences.en: Now, that era of quitting is over.
sentences.zh: 现在，那个辞职的时代已经结束了。

sentences.en: I'm Natalie Kittroweff.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·基特罗夫。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Ben Castleman on what its end means for workers.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事本·卡斯尔曼将探讨这一现象的终结对劳动者意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, July 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月12日，星期三。

sentences.en: Hi, Ben.
sentences.zh: 你好，本。

sentences.en: Natalie.
sentences.zh: 娜塔莉。

sentences.en: Ben, this is so fun.
sentences.zh: 本，这太有趣了。

sentences.en: This is the first time we've done a daily together.
sentences.zh: 这是我们第一次一起做《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: I'm genuinely really excited.
sentences.zh: 我真的非常兴奋。

sentences.en: I can't believe it.
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: Reunited.
sentences.zh: 重逢了。

sentences.en: It feels so good.
sentences.zh: 感觉真好。

sentences.en: So, back in 2021, you did an episode with us where we heard from all of these people who had left their jobs.
sentences.zh: 回到2021年，你曾和我们做过一期节目，当时我们听到了所有那些辞职的人的心声。

sentences.en: And then just last week, I saw that you wrote a story saying that that phenomenon, the Great Resignation, had ended.
sentences.zh: 就在上周，我看到你写了一篇报道，说那种现象，也就是“大辞职潮”，已经结束了。

sentences.en: What did you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: So, what I mean by that is that we had this period coming out of the pandemic of just rapid-fire job switching across the American economy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，疫情过后，我们经历了一段美国经济中频繁跳槽的时期。

sentences.en: And we can measure this directly because the government, the Bureau of Labor Statistics, measures how many people quit their jobs every month.
sentences.zh: 我们可以直接衡量这一点，因为政府的劳工统计局每个月都会统计有多少人辞职。

sentences.en: And that measure went through the roof coming out of the pandemic, and it stayed through the roof for months and months to an unprecedented level.
sentences.zh: 疫情过后，这一数据直线上升，并且在长达数月的时间里一直保持在史无前例的高位。

sentences.en: At the peak, four and a half million Americans a month were quitting their jobs.
sentences.zh: 在高峰期，每个月有450万美国人辞职。

sentences.en: But now it is coming down, and it has gotten pretty close to where it was before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但现在数据正在下降，已经非常接近疫情前的水平了。

sentences.en: So, I think we can safely say that the Great Resignation, whatever it was, is over.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为我们可以肯定地说，“大辞职潮”——无论它是什么——已经结束了。

sentences.en: And what are we supposed to make of that?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何理解这一点呢？

sentences.en: Why do we think that's happening?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们认为会发生这种情况？

sentences.en: Well, look, I mean, one possibility is that workers moved around and found jobs that they were happier with and that paid better.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，一种可能性是劳动者们四处流动，找到了让他们更满意、薪水更高的工作。

sentences.en: So, they don't need to keep moving because they got a job that they like.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们不需要再继续跳槽了，因为他们已经得到了自己喜欢的工作。

sentences.en: And I'm sure that for some people, that is what happened.
sentences.zh: 我相信对一些人来说，确实是这样。

sentences.en: But I think what's more likely in the economy as a whole is that a lot of workers are starting to feel nervous.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，从整个经济层面来看，更可能的情况是许多劳动者开始感到不安。

sentences.en: You know, we've been hearing for a long time now about the risks of a recession.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们很长一段时间以来一直在听关于经济衰退风险的警告。

sentences.en: I mean, we've talked about this on the Daily many times.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在《每日新闻》中多次讨论过这个问题。

sentences.en: Workers are aware of that.
sentences.zh: 劳动者们对此是有所察觉的。

sentences.en: They're hearing these warnings.
sentences.zh: 他们听到了这些警告。

sentences.en: They're seeing that the economy is not booming along the way it was coming out of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 他们看到经济不再像疫情刚结束时那样蓬勃发展了。

sentences.en: And so, I think we're starting to see evidence of workers getting just a little bit more cautious and not feeling like, oh, what,
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为我们开始看到劳动者变得更加谨慎的迹象，他们不再觉得，哦，什么，

sentences.en: they can just walk out the door and get something else.
sentences.zh: 他们可以随时甩手走人，再找一份别的工作。

sentences.en: It sounds to me like, honestly, in order to understand why the Great Resignation is over, we kind of need to understand why it happened in the first place.
sentences.zh: 老实说，在我看来，为了理解为什么“大辞职潮”会结束，我们需要先理解它当初为什么会发生。

sentences.en: Can you explain that?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: To us?
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm glad you asked because I think that this phrase, Great Resignation, honestly, I've never liked it very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，很高兴你问这个问题，因为老实说，我从来都不太喜欢“大辞职潮”这个词。

sentences.en: Because I think that it calls to mind a picture in a lot of people's heads that really doesn't reflect what was going on in reality.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为它在很多人脑海中唤起了一种画面，而这并不能反映现实中到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: You know, I think you hear Great Resignation and you think about people who are privileged white-collar professionals who, after the pandemic, are rethinking their priorities.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得当你听到“大辞职潮”时，你会想到那些享有特权的白领专业人士，他们在疫情后重新思考了自己的优先事项。

sentences.en: Or it's young people who, you know, just want to go and live van life in the country.
sentences.zh: 或者是一些年轻人，你知道，只想去乡下过那种房车生活。

sentences.en: And look, I think that did happen.
sentences.zh: 听着，我认为这种情况确实发生过。

sentences.en: We saw quits rise pretty much across all industries and all demographic groups.
sentences.zh: 我们看到几乎所有行业和所有人口群体的辞职率都在上升。

sentences.en: But that's not most of it.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是大部分情况。

sentences.en: That's not where it's concentrated.
sentences.zh: 这并不是它集中的地方。

sentences.en: To a large degree, the Great Resignation was a phenomenon of low-wage workers, of service workers, in hospitality, in leisure, in retail.
sentences.zh: 在很大程度上，“大辞职潮”是低薪劳动者、服务业劳动者、酒店业、休闲业和零售业劳动者的一种现象。

sentences.en: That's where the weight of the quitting was.
sentences.zh: 那才是辞职潮的重心所在。

sentences.en: And can you remind us why they were quitting?
sentences.zh: 你能提醒我们他们为什么要辞职吗？

sentences.en: So I think it helps to wind back the clock a bit to the pandemic period.
sentences.zh: 我认为把时间拨回到疫情期间会有所帮助。

sentences.en: We saw businesses shut down, especially in-person businesses, and lay off millions of workers, most of whom go on unemployment benefits,
sentences.zh: 我们看到企业倒闭，尤其是面对面的服务业，数百万工人被解雇，其中大多数人开始领取失业救济金，

sentences.en: which expanded significantly in the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这些救济金在疫情期间大幅增加了。

sentences.en: So that by the time we get to the spring of 2021 and vaccines are being rolled out, businesses are reopening, people are going back to restaurants and hotels and retail outlets,
sentences.zh: 所以到了2021年春天，疫苗开始推广，企业重新开业，人们回到餐馆、酒店和零售店，

sentences.en: all these businesses suddenly need workers.
sentences.zh: 所有这些企业突然都需要工人。

sentences.en: And for workers who were in these industries at that time, this was a pretty miserable moment, right?
sentences.zh: 对于当时身处这些行业的劳动者来说，这是一个非常痛苦的时刻，对吧？

sentences.en: This is when it still feels really unsafe in a lot of cases to do this work.
sentences.zh: 在很多情况下，从事这些工作仍然让人感到非常不安全。

sentences.en: It's a time where they're being asked to enforce mask mandates and are often getting a lot of pushback on that.
sentences.zh: 这是一个他们被要求强制执行口罩令，且经常遭到很多抵触的时期。

sentences.en: And look, that's only one of the reasons why the supply of workers was constrained.
sentences.zh: 听着，这只是劳动力供应受限的原因之一。

sentences.en: You know, child care was still disrupted, so a lot of people couldn't return for that reason.
sentences.zh: 你知道，托儿服务仍然中断，所以很多人因为这个原因无法重返工作岗位。

sentences.en: The borders were still, by and large, sealed.
sentences.zh: 边境在很大程度上仍然是封闭的。

sentences.en: So we lost out on what is usually a major source of low-wage work in this country, which is immigration.
sentences.zh: 所以我们失去了这个国家通常主要的低薪劳动力来源，也就是移民。

sentences.en: And so for all of these reasons, we had a ton of demand for workers as we all rushed back out into the world and not that much supply.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于所有这些原因，当我们所有人涌回世界时，对劳动力的需求巨大，而供应却不足。

sentences.en: But Ben, can I ask you, what about unemployment benefits that people were getting during and after the pandemic?
sentences.zh: 但是本，我可以问你，疫情期间及之后人们领取的失业救济金是怎么回事？

sentences.en: How did that play into any of this?
sentences.zh: 这在其中起了什么作用？

sentences.en: It's a really important question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的问题。

sentences.en: You know, one of the major policy tools that the government used during the pandemic was expanded unemployment benefits.
sentences.zh: 你知道，政府在疫情期间使用的主要政策工具之一就是扩大失业救济金。

sentences.en: For a while there, you were able to get an extra $600 a week in unemployment benefits.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，你每周可以额外获得600美元的失业救济金。

sentences.en: And this was done explicitly to try to give people an option not to work, right?
sentences.zh: 这样做明确是为了给人们一个不工作的选择，对吧？

sentences.en: This is at the heart of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这是疫情的核心所在。

sentences.en: We wanted people to be able to stay home and be safe.
sentences.zh: 我们希望人们能够待在家里，保持安全。

sentences.en: Those benefits continued in a somewhat reduced form after the economy began to reopen.
sentences.zh: 经济开始重新开放后，这些福利以某种缩减的形式继续存在。

sentences.en: And we began to hear a lot of businesses complaining that they couldn't find workers because the workers were out there receiving unemployment benefits.
sentences.zh: 我们开始听到许多企业抱怨说他们找不到工人，因为工人们都在外面领取失业救济金。

sentences.en: And we certainly know that unemployment benefits did give workers some more leverage in this situation, right?
sentences.zh: 我们当然知道，失业救济金确实让工人在这种情况下拥有了更多的筹码，对吧？

sentences.en: They didn't have to come back to the first job that was offered to them because they had a way of paying their rent and of buying food.
sentences.zh: 他们不必回到提供给他们的第一份工作，因为他们有办法支付房租和购买食物。

sentences.en: But we also know that the quitting that we've been talking about here actually continued to increase after those extra benefits expired, after they went away.
sentences.zh: 但我们也知道，我们在这里谈论的辞职现象，实际上在那些额外福利到期、消失之后仍在继续增加。

sentences.en: What we're seeing is workers quitting their jobs to go, in some cases,
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是，工人们辞职去，在某些情况下，

sentences.en: start businesses of their own or to change into other industries that maybe are more attractive to them at that point.
sentences.zh: 创办自己的企业，或者转行到其他在当时对他们来说更有吸引力的行业。

sentences.en: Or in many cases, to go into other businesses in their same industry.
sentences.zh: 或者在许多情况下，去同一行业的其他企业工作。

sentences.en: And so what we're talking about here, this great resignation period, it can't be about unemployment benefits, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我们在这里谈论的这个“大辞职潮”时期，不可能是因为失业救济金，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it continued to grow after the unemployment benefits went away.
sentences.zh: 因为它在失业救济金消失后仍在继续增长。

sentences.en: What does that tell you, Ben?
sentences.zh: 这说明了什么，本？

sentences.en: What was happening in the economy that explains that?
sentences.zh: 经济中发生了什么可以解释这一点？

sentences.en: What it tells me is that this was still a moment of really intense demand for workers and that it became a real moment of worker power.
sentences.zh: 它告诉我的事，这仍然是一个对劳动力需求非常强烈的时刻，它成为了一个真正的劳动者力量崛起的时刻。

sentences.en: These businesses wanted workers.
sentences.zh: 这些企业想要工人。

sentences.en: They needed workers.
sentences.zh: 他们需要工人。

sentences.en: And a lot of workers had moved on and gone on to other industries.
sentences.zh: 而许多工人已经跳槽去了其他行业。

sentences.en: And as a result, the workers who were left behind had some leverage.
sentences.zh: 结果，留下的工人就有了一些筹码。

sentences.en: They had the ability to say, I'm not going to come work for you if you're going to pay me the $12 an hour that you were paying me before.
sentences.zh: 他们有能力说：如果你只付给我以前那每小时12美元的工资，我就不会来为你工作。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think there's also an important element of psychology, of workers sort of discovering a power that maybe on some level they already had, but now they knew about.
sentences.zh: 我认为还有一个重要的心理因素，即劳动者们发现了一种他们可能在某种程度上已经拥有，但现在才意识到的力量。

sentences.en: You know, once they had quit a job to go take another job, maybe it's not as hard to do it a second time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一旦他们辞掉一份工作去接受另一份工作，也许第二次做起来就不那么难了。

sentences.en: Maybe they can go to their boss and say, listen, you know how you hired me away from somewhere else?
sentences.zh: 也许他们可以去找老板说：听着，你知道你是怎么把我从别处挖过来的吗？

sentences.en: Someone else can do that.
sentences.zh: 别人也能做到这一点。

sentences.en: So you better give me that $1 an hour raise.
sentences.zh: 所以你最好给我每小时加薪1美元。

sentences.en: I think we had a real sort of bubbling up of worker consciousness that they held some power in this negotiation.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们确实出现了一种劳动者意识的觉醒，即他们在这场谈判中拥有一定的力量。

sentences.en: And that fundamental power shift, does it have an impact on the economy?
sentences.zh: 这种根本性的权力转移，会对经济产生影响吗？

sentences.en: Can you see it play out?
sentences.zh: 你能看到它的影响吗？

sentences.en: You can see it clear as day.
sentences.zh: 你可以看得一清二楚。

sentences.en: The most obvious place is in wages.
sentences.zh: 最明显的地方就是工资。

sentences.en: What we saw in this period was pay for these low-wage workers going way up.
sentences.zh: 我们在这一时期看到的是，这些低薪工人的工资大幅上涨。

sentences.en: I think over a two-year period, we saw something like a 28% increase in hourly earnings for hotel and restaurant workers,
sentences.zh: 我认为在两年时间里，酒店和餐饮业工人的时薪增长了大约28%，

sentences.en: which shows that employers really needed workers and they were willing to pay for them.
sentences.zh: 这表明雇主确实需要工人，而且他们愿意为此买单。

sentences.en: And Ben, put that into context for me.
sentences.zh: 本，帮我把这个放在背景中看一看。

sentences.en: How big of a deal is that increase in wages, given what we have seen over the last several decades in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 考虑到过去几十年来我们在美国经济中看到的情况，工资的这种增长有多重要？

sentences.en: economy?
sentences.zh: 经济。

sentences.en: It's a sea change.
sentences.zh: 这是一场巨变。

sentences.en: I've been covering economics for 15 years now.
sentences.zh: 我报道经济新闻已经15年了。

sentences.en: And for as long as I've been covering this, we've been talking about wage stagnation and how wages, especially for the lowest-wage workers, have just been stuck.
sentences.zh: 在我报道经济的这段时间里，我们一直在谈论工资停滞，以及工资，尤其是最低工资工人的工资，是如何一直停滞不前的。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, they came unstuck.
sentences.zh: 而突然之间，它们不再停滞了。

sentences.en: We saw wages for low-wage workers rise faster than for any other group.
sentences.zh: 我们看到低薪工人的工资增长速度超过了任何其他群体。

sentences.en: And it actually reduced in a significant way the inequality, the gap between what the highest earners make and what the lowest earners make.
sentences.zh: 它实际上显著减少了不平等，即最高收入者和最低收入者之间的差距。

sentences.en: Economists have been studying this.
sentences.zh: 经济学家们一直在研究这个问题。

sentences.en: And over the last couple of years, we've reversed about a quarter of the 40-year increase in earnings inequality.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，我们扭转了过去40年收入不平等增长的大约四分之一。

sentences.en: That's obviously not 100% of it or close to it, but it's a really big bite to take in just a two-year period.
sentences.zh: 这显然不是100%，甚至不接近，但在短短两年内，这是一个非常大的进步。

sentences.en: And now, you've told us, the quit rate is almost back to where it was pre-pandemic.
sentences.zh: 现在，你告诉我们，辞职率几乎回到了疫情前的水平。

sentences.en: This period, this great resignation, is over.
sentences.zh: 这个时期，这个“大辞职潮”，已经结束了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The period of quitting, the great resignation period, seems to be, by and large, behind us.
sentences.zh: 辞职的时期，也就是“大辞职潮”时期，似乎在很大程度上已经成为过去。

sentences.en: And so, I think that the logical question now is whether this moment of worker power is also behind us.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为现在合乎逻辑的问题是，这种劳动者力量崛起的时刻是否也已经成为过去。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Ben, before the break, you hinted at the fact that the increase in earnings, especially among low-wage workers, might not last with the end of the great resignation.
sentences.zh: 本，在休息之前，你暗示过这样一个事实：随着“大辞职潮”的结束，收入的增长，尤其是低薪工人的收入增长，可能无法持续。

sentences.en: Tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 能详细说说吗？

sentences.en: So, all of these gains that we've seen, they've basically come as a result of a really hot labor market, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，我们所看到的这些收益，基本上都是源于一个非常火热的劳动力市场，对吧？

sentences.en: Of lots of demand for workers, outstripping supply, giving workers leverage.
sentences.zh: 对工人的需求很大，超过了供给，这给了工人议价能力。

sentences.en: But inevitably, at some point, the labor market will not be so strong, right?
sentences.zh: 但不可避免的是，在某个时刻，劳动力市场将不会那么强劲，对吧？

sentences.en: Unemployment will rise.
sentences.zh: 失业率将会上升。

sentences.en: We'll hit a recession, whenever that may be.
sentences.zh: 无论何时，我们终将遭遇经济衰退。

sentences.en: And nothing has happened to lock in these gains so that these gains will persist beyond just a strong labor market.
sentences.zh: 而且目前没有任何措施来锁定这些收益，使它们在强劲的劳动力市场之外依然能够持续。

sentences.en: What could we have done?
sentences.zh: 我们本可以做些什么呢？

sentences.en: So, your answer to that, of course, is going to depend on your political perspective, your approach to the economy, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，这个问题的答案当然取决于你的政治观点和你的经济方针，对吧？

sentences.en: Folks on the left are going to point to things like the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 左翼人士会指出最低工资之类的问题。

sentences.en: Wages across the country are now far above, in practice, right?
sentences.zh: 实际上，全国各地的工资水平现在已经远高于此了，对吧？

sentences.en: Wages are far above the federal minimum wage of $7.25.
sentences.zh: 工资水平远高于每小时7.25美元的联邦最低工资标准。

sentences.en: But the federal minimum wage hasn't gone up.
sentences.zh: 但联邦最低工资标准却一直没有提高。

sentences.en: And so, the moment that the economy gets weaker, right, employers could just try to pay that $7.25 an hour minimum wage again.
sentences.zh: 所以，一旦经济变弱，雇主们可能就会再次尝试支付每小时7.25美元的最低工资。

sentences.en: We haven't seen policies to make it easier for workers to organize.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有看到能让工人更容易组织起来的政策。

sentences.en: We haven't expanded unemployment benefits, for example, in a way that gives workers an opportunity to hold out for a better job if they lose their job.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们没有扩大失业救济金，以至于工人在失业时没有机会等待更好的工作机会。

sentences.en: So, we haven't seen sort of any of the kind of policies that folks on the left think would help strengthen workers' power in some more enduring way.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们还没有看到左翼人士认为能以更持久的方式加强工人力量的那类政策。

sentences.en: And we haven't seen any of the policies that folks on the right might point to either.
sentences.zh: 我们也同样没有看到右翼人士可能指出的任何政策。

sentences.en: You know, as a general rule, people on the right are less likely to see inequality per se as a problem.
sentences.zh: 你知道，作为一般规则，右翼人士不太可能将不平等本身视为一个问题。

sentences.en: But there are certainly steps that they would like to see the government take that they argue would help workers over the long run, things to make it easier to start a business,
sentences.zh: 但他们肯定希望政府采取一些他们认为从长远来看有助于工人的措施，比如让创业变得更容易，

sentences.en: things to make it easier to change jobs by lowering licensing requirements, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如通过降低许可要求来让换工作变得更容易。

sentences.en: You know, we haven't seen those kinds of policies either.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们也没有看到那类政策。

sentences.en: And so, what we're left with here is a system that just depends on the strength of the economy, that isn't dependent on any policies that would help kind of lock in these gains.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们现在面对的是一个仅仅依赖于经济强弱的体系，它并不依赖于任何有助于锁定这些收益的政策。

sentences.en: What you're saying is that neither side, not the left, not the right, no one,
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，无论是哪一方，左派还是右派，没有人，

sentences.en: has been able to take advantage of this moment where workers had real leverage to put in place policies that would have made some of these gains more permanent.
sentences.zh: 能够利用工人拥有真正议价能力的这一时刻，去实施那些能让这些收益更持久的政策。

sentences.en: Yeah, you might think that this would have been the moment to do that.
sentences.zh: 是的，你可能会认为这本该是采取行动的时刻。

sentences.en: If you ever think it makes sense to raise the minimum wage,
sentences.zh: 如果你认为提高最低工资是有意义的，

sentences.en: it would make sense in a period where real-world wages have outstripped the minimum wage to such a degree that it literally wouldn't cost businesses anything to raise the minimum.
sentences.zh: 那么在实际工资已经大幅超过最低工资的时期，这样做是有意义的，因为提高最低工资实际上根本不会增加企业的成本。

sentences.en: If you think that there are policies that would help workers, it sort of makes sense to put them into a place during a good economy.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为有些政策能帮助工人，那么在经济形势好的时候实施它们是有道理的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Not to wait around and try to do it in the middle of a recession when businesses are trying to survive.
sentences.zh: 而不是等到经济衰退、企业都在努力生存的时候才去尝试。

sentences.en: But we haven't done any of that.
sentences.zh: 但我们什么都没做。

sentences.en: And why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Well, look, if you talk to folks in the Biden administration, for example,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，如果你去和拜登政府的人谈，

sentences.en: they'll point to all sorts of things that they've done that they would argue will help the economy and help workers in the long run, right?
sentences.zh: 他们会列举出他们所做的各种事情，并认为这些事情从长远来看有助于经济和工人，对吧？

sentences.en: Their infrastructure bill, for example, all of these kinds of policies that they argue will make the economy stronger.
sentences.zh: 比如他们的基础设施法案，所有这些他们认为会让经济更强劲的政策。

sentences.en: But a lot of things that they tried to do in terms of raising the minimum wage and in terms of unionization policies, right, those are things that didn't get through Congress.
sentences.zh: 但他们在提高最低工资和工会化政策方面尝试做的很多事情，那些都没能在国会通过。

sentences.en: And the idea of gridlocking Congress is hardly new and not something I think you and I are going to solve here.
sentences.zh: 国会陷入僵局的想法并不新鲜，也不是你我在这里就能解决的问题。

sentences.en: But it's a reality that has limited what the government has been able to do during this period.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是一个限制了政府在此期间所能作为的现实。

sentences.en: So, Ben, where do we go from here?
sentences.zh: 那么，本，接下来我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: So a lot is going to depend on the economy.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上取决于经济。

sentences.en: And right now, the labor market remains strong.
sentences.zh: 目前，劳动力市场依然强劲。

sentences.en: The unemployment rate is still very low.
sentences.zh: 失业率仍然很低。

sentences.en: We're still adding jobs at a pretty steady rate.
sentences.zh: 我们依然以相当稳定的速度在增加就业岗位。

sentences.en: Wages are still rising.
sentences.zh: 工资仍在上涨。

sentences.en: They're no longer rising faster for workers at the bottom of the pay scale, but they're still rising for pretty much everybody.
sentences.zh: 虽然工资水平处于底层的工人的工资不再上涨得那么快，但对几乎所有人来说，工资仍在上涨。

sentences.en: So as long as that continues, we have no reason to think workers will lose the gains that they've already made, even if they're not continuing to make huge additional gains.
sentences.zh: 所以只要这种情况持续下去，我们就没有理由认为工人会失去他们已经获得的收益，即使他们不再继续获得巨大的额外收益。

sentences.en: But look, the economy is vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 但你看，经济是脆弱的。

sentences.en: Forecasters have been predicting a recession for months now, and it keeps not coming.
sentences.zh: 预测者们几个月来一直在预测经济衰退，但它一直没有到来。

sentences.en: But at some point, it may.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时刻，它可能会来。

sentences.en: The Fed has been raising interest rates aggressively.
sentences.zh: 美联储一直在激进地提高利率。

sentences.en: We've seen certainly a slowdown in the economy, even if it's at this point still in decent shape.
sentences.zh: 我们确实看到了经济放缓，即使目前经济状况尚可。

sentences.en: And look, there will be a recession one of these days.
sentences.zh: 而且，总有一天会发生经济衰退。

sentences.en: And because we don't have anything that has sort of locked in these gains, when that happens, there's a real possibility that a lot of what workers have seen here will disappear,
sentences.zh: 由于我们没有任何锁定这些收益的措施，当衰退发生时，工人所看到的很多东西很有可能会消失，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: If all of their leverage came from this huge demand for workers, then it's going to disappear when that demand goes away.
sentences.zh: 如果他们所有的议价能力都来自对工人的巨大需求，那么当这种需求消失时，这些能力也会随之消失。

sentences.en: So in the economy that we're in now,
sentences.zh: 那么在我们现在的经济中，

sentences.en: where there is a lot of talk of a coming recession and where there's no policies on the left or the right that would keep the concrete gains going,
sentences.zh: 关于即将到来的经济衰退的讨论很多，而且左派或右派都没有能让具体收益持续下去的政策，

sentences.en: what happens to the other piece of this that you were talking about?
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到的另一部分会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: This new sense of consciousness among workers, that feeling of worker power.
sentences.zh: 这种工人中产生的新意识，那种工人力量的感觉。

sentences.en: I think in some ways that's the most interesting question here.
sentences.zh: 我认为在某些方面，这是这里最有趣的问题。

sentences.en: It's also, in some ways, the hardest to answer, right?
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这也是最难回答的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's hard to measure.
sentences.zh: 因为它很难衡量。

sentences.en: But I think there is a real sense that this period has been a wake-up call for workers and a moment of real mobilization.
sentences.zh: 但我认为确实有一种感觉，这段时期对工人来说是一个警钟，也是一个真正动员的时刻。

sentences.en: You see that in a direct way in unionization, right?
sentences.zh: 你在工会化方面直接看到了这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: We've seen unionization drives at Starbucks and at Amazon.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了星巴克和亚马逊的工会化运动。

sentences.en: We see strike activity, whether it's the Hollywood writer's strike that's going on now or a UPS strike that's looming on the horizon.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了罢工活动，无论是现在正在进行的好莱坞编剧罢工，还是即将到来的UPS罢工。

sentences.en: But we also see it not just in this sort of classic organized labor way, but also just in sort of the day-to-day activity and awareness of individual workers.
sentences.zh: 但我们看到的不仅仅是这种传统的有组织劳工方式，还有个体工人的日常活动和意识。

sentences.en: I talk to a lot of low-wage workers, and a lot of them tell me that this period has changed the way they think about their work and their role in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 我和许多低薪工人交谈过，他们中的许多人告诉我，这段时期改变了他们对工作以及自己在工作场所角色的看法。

sentences.en: They've had this moment of realizing, I can go to my boss and I can say, if you don't give me a raise, I'm going to go down the street and get a different job, get a better job.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到：我可以去找老板说，如果你不给我加薪，我就去街对面找另一份工作，找一份更好的工作。

sentences.en: And once that awareness exists, it changes the way they think.
sentences.zh: 一旦这种意识存在，它就会改变他们的思维方式。

sentences.en: And it is a lesson that they say they're not going to forget anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 而且他们说，这是一个他们不会很快忘记的教训。

sentences.en: But will they be able to actually use those lessons if the economy goes south?
sentences.zh: 但如果经济恶化，他们真的能运用这些经验吗？

sentences.en: I mean, if things get really desperate, if there are fewer jobs out there, how do workers use this consciousness?
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果情况变得非常绝望，如果工作机会变少了，工人们该如何运用这种意识？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's a really fair question.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一个非常公平的问题。

sentences.en: If most of this power came from an ability to go to your boss and say, give me a raise or else, right, what happens when the boss chooses or else?
sentences.zh: 如果这种力量大部分来自你可以去找老板说“不加薪就走人”的能力，那么当老板选择“走人”时会发生什么？

sentences.en: What happens when the boss says, fine, we were about to lay people off anyway, so walk away?
sentences.zh: 当老板说“好吧，反正我们本来也要裁员，那就走吧”时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: If we haven't seen any real structural shifts here, and if we haven't seen any real policy shifts,
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有看到任何真正的结构性转变，也没有看到任何真正的政策转变，

sentences.en: then I don't know why we should expect these gains to last in a period of high unemployment, of few job opportunities, in a real recession.
sentences.zh: 那么我不知道为什么我们应该期待这些收益在失业率高、工作机会少、真正的经济衰退时期能够持续下去。

sentences.en: That makes me wonder, Ben, what is the long-term impact then of the Great Resignation?
sentences.zh: 这让我不禁想问，本，那么“大辞职潮”的长期影响是什么？

sentences.en: So, look, workers right now are still being paid significantly better, particularly low-wage workers, significantly better than they were before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 你看，工人们现在的工资确实比疫情前高得多，尤其是低薪工人，比以前好多了。

sentences.en: You know, there's a universe here where, at the very least, workers hold on to some of those gains.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一种可能，至少工人们能保住其中的一些收益。

sentences.en: Maybe they don't make further gains, but at least we see a higher floor for a lot of workers going forward.
sentences.zh: 也许他们不会获得进一步的收益，但至少我们看到未来很多工人的工资底线提高了。

sentences.en: And so, has the Great Resignation changed things in a lasting way?
sentences.zh: 那么，“大辞职潮”是否以一种持久的方式改变了现状？

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: If you talk to some workers, if you talk to some union organizers, they'll argue yes.
sentences.zh: 如果你和一些工人谈，如果你和一些工会组织者谈，他们会说是的。

sentences.en: But I think the test of that is going to come whenever that recession hits, and history tells us that it will hit someday.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，无论何时经济衰退到来，历史告诉我们它终会到来，那将是对此的考验。

sentences.en: Then we'll see whether these gains hold up or if they disappear just like the Great Resignation has.
sentences.zh: 到那时我们就会看到这些收益是否能保持住，还是会像“大辞职潮”一样消失。

sentences.en: Ben, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 本，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Natalie.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，娜塔莉。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times Games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的“Connections”谜题，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责制作“Spelling Bee”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人们制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: A federal judge cleared the way for Microsoft to buy Activision Blizzard, blocking an attempt by the Federal Trade Commission to delay the merger.
sentences.zh: 一位联邦法官为微软收购动视暴雪扫清了障碍，阻止了联邦贸易委员会推迟合并的企图。

sentences.en: The FTC failed to convince the judge that it could prove that the merger between Microsoft, which makes the Xbox, and Activision, which makes video games,
sentences.zh: 联邦贸易委员会未能说服法官，证明它能证明微软（Xbox的制造商）与动视（视频游戏的制造商）之间的合并，

sentences.en: would reduce competition and hurt consumers.
sentences.zh: 会减少竞争并损害消费者利益。

sentences.en: The ruling was the latest setback for the FTC, which has tried to become more aggressive in policing big tech, but has not yet won any major victories in court.
sentences.zh: 这一裁决是联邦贸易委员会遭遇的最新挫折，该委员会一直试图在监管大型科技公司方面变得更加激进，但尚未在法庭上赢得任何重大胜利。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 还有……

sentences.en: Make no mistake, the devastation and flooding we're experiencing across Vermont is historic and catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，我们正在佛蒙特州经历的破坏和洪水是历史性的、灾难性的。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, the governor of Vermont, Phil Scott, warned residents that even though the rainfall that had pummeled the state had subsided, the flooding still isn't over.
sentences.zh: 周二，佛蒙特州州长菲尔·斯科特警告居民，尽管袭击该州的降雨已经减弱，但洪水仍未结束。

sentences.en: Flood waters continue to rise in some places, like our capital city, and have surpassed the levels seen during Tropical Storm Irene.
sentences.zh: 洪水在一些地方（如我们的首府）继续上涨，并已超过了热带风暴艾琳期间的水平。

sentences.en: Rivers in the state reached some of their highest levels on record, while the authorities worked furiously to reach people stranded in remote mountain towns.
sentences.zh: 该州的河流达到了有记录以来的最高水位，当局正全力营救被困在偏远山镇的人们。

sentences.en: By Tuesday, they had rescued at least 117 people from cars and homes.
sentences.zh: 到周二，他们已经从汽车和房屋中救出了至少117人。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Shannon Lynn and Carlos Prieto, with help from Michael Simon Johnson.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由香农·林恩和卡洛斯·普列托制作，迈克尔·西蒙·约翰逊提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow, with help from Mark George.
sentences.zh: 由丽莎·周编辑，马克·乔治提供了帮助。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Marion Lozano, and was engineered by Alyssa Jane Moxley.
sentences.zh: 包含玛丽昂·洛萨诺的原创音乐，由艾丽莎·简·莫克斯利进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Natalie Ketrowet.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·凯特罗韦特。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序上或你喜欢的任何地方收听《Wirecutter秀》。
